title: Callers converge on one datastore that answers slowly while sitting idle

problem.summary: Several services slow down at once and their slow call paths all end at the same downstream datastore. The datastore is not busy: its CPU, disk and memory are quiet, and it emits no request traces of its own, so ordinary telemetry points at its callers instead of at it. The callers are victims; the datastore is spending its time blocked on something outside itself.
symptoms: caller latency inflates sharply, often by orders of magnitude
the slow call edges all converge on one shared downstream component
that component is resource-quiet: CPU flat or falling, no disk or memory pressure
requests still succeed, so error rates barely move

discriminators.signal: kernel wait decomposition of the converged-on component
discriminators.this_problem: off_cpu_io_wait dominates while on_cpu stays near zero: it is blocked waiting on something external, not working
discriminators.not_this_problem: runnable_wait rises, which means it is ready to run but starved of CPU

discriminators.this_problem: the suspect has slow INCOMING edges only; its own outgoing edges are normal, or it emits no spans at all
discriminators.not_this_problem: its outgoing edges are also slow, in which case the real cause is further downstream and you should keep walking

discriminators.this_problem: traffic continues and succeeds, just slowly
discriminators.not_this_problem: calls fail or hang to timeout and the component serves little successful traffic

discriminators.this_problem: the datastore path dominates while service-to-service hops stay comparatively healthy
discriminators.not_this_problem: every hop slows by a similar factor, which points at the network rather than the datastore

reproduction.system: Sock Shop or Train Ticket on Ubuntu 24.04, LTTng 2.15, Docker 27+, single GCP n2 VM. Toxiproxy sits permanently in the datastore path so latency can be toggled without restarting anything.

logs: error-rate change per container, to confirm calls succeed rather than fail
traces: caller to callee edge latency, baseline versus incident, so convergence can be seen
collection_order.why_these: Unlike the CPU-contention blueprint, this one DOES need syscall entry and exit events: the verdict depends on which syscall the thread was blocked in when it left the CPU. sched_switch alone tells you it stopped running; the open syscall tells you it stopped to wait on the network or a socket rather than on disk or a lock. That distinction is the whole diagnosis, so the cheaper scheduler-only order is not sufficient here.

processing.step: Stage the kernel trace so babeltrace2 can read it, because channels are stored gzipped
processing.expect: a CTF directory containing a metadata file and channel0_* streams

processing.step: Find which downstream component the slow call edges converge on
processing.expect: one component with slow incoming edges and no slow outgoing edges; if several, take the deepest

processing.step: Decode scheduler and syscall events for the suspect inside the incident window
processing.expect: non-empty output; zero lines means the window is misaligned, because the trace is stamped in the host timezone while ground truth is UTC, so TZ=UTC is required

processing.step: Attribute the suspect wall time across on-CPU, runnable-wait, disk-wait and external I/O wait
processing.expect: off_cpu_io_wait dominant, on_cpu near zero, and a verdict_hint of external_io_or_dependency_wait

processing.step: Confirm the suspect is unsaturated, then emit the verdict and its artifacts
processing.expect: the suspect shows external wait without CPU, disk or memory saturation

outputs.contains: the converged-on component, its wait decomposition, the slowdown factor on its incoming edges, and the resource signals that rule out saturation
the four wait shares for the suspect over time, with the incident window shaded
which component was waiting, on what, and why its callers are victims rather than causes

verdict_when: slow call edges converge on one component that has no slow outgoing edges
that component shows dominant off-CPU external I/O wait with a near-zero on-CPU share
it is resource-quiet: no CPU, disk or memory saturation
traffic continues to succeed, so error rates barely move

rule_out.when: calls fail or hang to timeout and the component serves little successful traffic
block latency is up host-wide and other disk users degrade too
the suspect shows runnable_wait rather than external I/O wait
every hop slows by a similar factor, not just the datastore path

decision.root_cause_is: the converged-on datastore component itself, never its callers, which are victims

evidence_from_literature.claim: Blocking-syscall attribution distinguishes a component that is slow from a component that is waiting, which utilisation metrics cannot do
evidence_from_literature.validated_on: our labelled slow-datastore runs; on Sock Shop this verdict survives even with traces removed entirely

provenance.notes: Deliberately the mirror image of the CPU-contention blueprint. Same tool, same trace, opposite verdict, and the two collection orders differ in a way that matters: this one needs syscall events, the other does not.
